scenes.name: hook
scenes.text: Every bill you pay has a line that says GST. But who actually pays it, and why isn't it taxed again and again?

scenes.name: what
scenes.text: GST is the goods and services tax. One tax on things you buy, replacing many older taxes in India.

scenes.name: chain
scenes.text: It's charged at each step of the chain. From raw material maker, to manufacturer, to shop.

scenes.name: credit
scenes.text: Each business subtracts the GST it already paid on its inputs. This is called input tax credit.

scenes.name: value
scenes.text: So at every step, tax is effectively paid only on the value added, not on tax over tax.

scenes.name: consumer
scenes.text: In the end, the full tax is carried by the final buyer. That's you, at the counter.

scenes.name: split
scenes.text: For sales within a state, it's split between the centre and the state, as CGST and SGST.

scenes.name: outro
scenes.text: Charged at each step, credit for tax paid, final buyer pays. Follow for more on how things really work.
